newsitem.title: UK: LCE white sugar races higher with New York raws.
newsitem.headline: LCE white sugar races higher with New York raws.

text.p: White sugar futures on the London Commodity Exchange (LCE) ended a busy day with sizeable gains, pushed higher during the last few hours of business by a surging raw sugar market in New York.
Turnover was an impressive 4,597 lots of which around half traded on the nearby October contract.
October finished $2.70 higher at $353.00 a tonne, while December rose $2.00 to $348.00.
Traders in London saw good October/December spread trading and crossed October against actuals business.
Raw sugar in New York surged, with CSCE October hitting a high of 12.20 cents a pound, the highest level seen since January 1995. It eased slightly by the close.
U.S. dealers attributed the rise to waves of fund buying.
Paris sugar also rose in response to New York, with October ending $2.50 higher at $353.00. Total turnover was 1,640 lots.
